summary: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Leading networks decide returnability early, capture disposition as structured data, and treat the return stream as a quality feedback loop rather than a cost to be administered.

leading_practices.title: Decide returnability at the point of diagnosis
leading_practices.description: The judgement about whether a part should travel is made in the workshop, guided by the system, so invalid returns never enter the network.

evidence.quote: Leaders decide returnability at the point of diagnosis, before the part leaves the dealership.

leading_practices.title: Structured disposition coding
leading_practices.description: Inspection outcomes are captured as codes against a controlled vocabulary instead of free text, making the return stream analysable.

evidence.quote: Structured disposition codes allow the return stream to be analysed as a quality signal.

leading_practices.title: Settlement speed as a dealer loyalty lever
leading_practices.description: Claims settle within 5 days at leading players and fill rate improves as a result.

evidence.quote: Leaders decide returnability at the point of diagnosis, before the part leaves the dealership.

common_operating_models: Regional return centres with a single technical inspection authority per region
Dealer self-service for initiation and status, with exception handling by a central team
automation_and_digital_enablers: Guided diagnosis at the dealer that gates the return request
Photographic evidence captured at initiation and carried through inspection
Status visibility shared with the dealer from initiation to settlement
risks_and_failure_modes: Free-text defect capture that cannot be analysed
Inspection evidence held outside the system of record, which drives disputes
Return decisions made after transport has already been paid for
